clue.text: Buzzer happened to be quiet

parts.note: past tense of 'be', so happened to be gives was
P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for quiet

explanation.surface: A doorbell or alarm that happened to stay silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasp is an insect that hums as it flies, so a buzzer in the cryptic sense.

clue.text: Take care of timekeeper on the other side

parts.note: a watch is a portable timepiece
over means across or on the far side

explanation.surface: Looking after a clock across the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To guard or protect someone, keeping an eye on them.

clue.text: Fine and ready with charity bazaar

parts.note: set means prepared, as in ready, steady
a fair is a fete or sale held for good causes

explanation.surface: Good weather and preparedness for a church fete.
explanation.definitionFit: Set fair describes settled good weather.

clue.text: Introduction given by Romeo in verse

indicators.note: the word in says the Romeo letter sits inside the verse word

parts.note: a poem is a piece of verse
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A prologue delivered by Shakespeare's Romeo in rhyming lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A proem is a preface or preamble to a book or speech.

clue.text: Dispose of rapidly when shine has disappeared

parts.note: polish is shine or lustre
off means gone or departed

explanation.surface: Getting rid of something quickly once its gloss is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish off is to finish or consume something quickly.

clue.text: Oedipus struggled during liturgical worship

indicators.note: struggled shows the letters wrestling into a new order

explanation.surface: The tragic king fought on through a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: Opus Dei literally means 'work of God', a name for the divine office of liturgical prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Benedictine usage the Latin phrase names the daily round of liturgical prayer.

clue.text: Some confusion about second prophet

indicators.note: about tells us the jumble goes around the second letter
confusion of the word some means its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Some muddle over a second seer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusion' turns SOME into MOES, and 'about' wraps that around S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrew leader who received the Ten Commandments is counted a prophet.

clue.text: It, note, will satisfy fully

parts.note: 'It' is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A remark that a single note will be completely satisfying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' in the sense of sex appeal (the 1920s 'It girl') gives SA, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: To glut or fill someone to capacity, as with food.

clue.text: It's about Greek character, after the usual time, to rouse

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so it's is read backwards

parts.note: the apostrophe gives no letter
mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
late means past the expected time

explanation.surface: Someone tardy is woken up by a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To stimulate is to excite or arouse into action.

clue.text: Downtrodden machine operator

parts.note: a foot-worked lever that drives a sewing machine or lathe, literally trodden down

explanation.definitionFit: A foot pedal that powers a machine such as an old sewing machine is pressed down by foot.

clue.text: Like a couple of nudists presumably — completely incompatible

definitions.text: Like a couple of nudists presumably

explanation.surface: Two naked people would make an ill-matched pair.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, nudists are wholly without suits; the phrase also means utterly ill-matched.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudists wear no clothing at all, while the everyday sense is being entirely wrong for each other or for a role.

clue.text: A hut is removed creating break in the series

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are shifted from their places and rearranged

explanation.surface: Taking down a shed causes an interruption in a run of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' is read as re-moved, moved about, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiatus is a gap or pause in a sequence or continuity.

clue.text: Sue'd said another is to discourage one from doing something

indicators.note: another version of the letters, i.e. a rearrangement

parts.note: Sue'd is the past tense sued, the apostrophe giving no letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A garbled line about someone who sued, meaning to talk a person out of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' asks for a different arrangement of SUED and SAID.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissuade is to persuade a person against a course of action.

clue.text: Our visit unsettled musicians

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Accomplished players were thrown by our trip to see them.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtuosi are highly skilled performers, especially of music.

clue.text: Estate managed with this money

parts.note: money placed in an arrangement where trustees manage the assets for a beneficiary

explanation.definitionFit: Assets held and administered by trustees on someone's behalf.

clue.text: (A)light jacket?

parts.note: read with the bracketed letter, something on fire; read without it, a coat that is not heavy

explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed A lets the clue be read two ways: a jacket that is not heavy, or something on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A blazer is a lightweight jacket, and jokingly anything that blazes, i.e. is on fire.

clue.text: Following rules exactly according to printed work

explanation.surface: Doing things strictly, as the manual says.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means strictly following procedure; literally it means as stated in a written volume.

clue.text: Journalists during rush had been restrained

indicators.note: during places the journalists word within the rush word

parts.note: a reed or rush is a marsh plant
the press is a collective term for journalists

explanation.surface: Reporters in a hurry had been held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rush' is the waterside plant, not haste.
explanation.definitionFit: Repressed means held in check or suppressed.

clue.text: Unexpected refusal of enthusiast

parts.note: of in the sense concerning or about gives re
a buff is a keen fan, as in film buff

explanation.surface: A fan being surprisingly turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuff is an abrupt, often unexpected snub or rejection.

clue.text: Unaccompanied cellist?

parts.note: not a solo musician but a solitary person living alone in a cell

explanation.walkthrough: 'cellist' suggests a musician; here it is someone who lives in a cell.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a hermit or religious recluse, who lives alone in a cell.

clue.text: Spread on top flatter

parts.note: butter is a spread for bread
up means above or on top

explanation.surface: Putting a spread on the top of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To butter up is to charm someone with praise to win favour.

clue.text: Pop group, one entering fair

indicators.note: entering shows the one letter going into the fair word

parts.note: blonde means fair-haired
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A band, one of them going into a fete.
explanation.definitionFit: Blondie is the American new-wave band fronted by Debbie Harry.

clue.text: Girl about to be with hundreds and one more

parts.note: re means about or concerning
taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so CC is hundreds
a means one

explanation.surface: A young woman is set to join hundreds plus one more.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebecca is a female first name.

clue.text: Nurse has attempt to pass old watchtower

parts.note: SEN stands for State Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade
a try is an attempt
go is a turn, as is a pass in a game

explanation.surface: A nurse tries to get past an ancient lookout post.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is best read as 'old watch tour': sentry-go is a dated military term for a sentry's duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentry-go is an old term for a guard's spell of duty, keeping watch.

clue.text: Loafers use it to get a rise

definitions.text: Loafers use it to get a rise

parts.words: Loafers use it to get a rise
parts.note: not idlers but makers of loaves, who need a raising agent for the dough

explanation.walkthrough: 'Loafers' suggests lazy people; here they are bakers making loaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Bakers add this fungus to dough so that bread rises.

clue.text: Provide someone with the means when ablest are included

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words when ablest

explanation.surface: Giving people resources when the most capable are part of the group.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable is to give someone the power or wherewithal to do something.

clue.text: Turin custodians performing play

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters are put through their paces in a new order

explanation.surface: Museum guards in an Italian city putting on a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloody early tragedy by Shakespeare about a Roman general.

clue.text: Troublesome plant, very small, died

parts.note: wee is Scottish for tiny
d is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A nuisance seedling, tiny, has withered.
explanation.definitionFit: A weed is any unwanted wild plant growing where it is not wanted.

clue.text: Pinch wife in wood

indicators.note: the word in places the wife letter within the wood word

parts.note: teak is a hard tropical timber

explanation.surface: Squeezing one's spouse in a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweak is a sharp twist or squeeze, as of a nose or cheek.

clue.text: One under a guardian fought, it is heard

indicators.note: the clue says the word for fought is to be spoken, giving a word sounding the same

parts.note: warred means fought a war

explanation.surface: A child in someone's care had a quarrel, by all reports.
explanation.definitionFit: A ward is a minor placed in the legal care of a guardian or court.
